taxonomic_note: Accepted species; Kew gives a native range from Texas to northeastern Mexico.
look_here_first: Find ONE entire leaf: S. pilosior has only ONE PAIR of comparatively broad hairy leaflets, approximately 1.3–1.8 times as long as wide. Check for short retrorse hairs and much stiffer long setae on stems, the gland where both leaflets meet, then anthers and hairy upright fruit. Do not separate by annual versus perennial habit: current sources disagree on its life history.

project_inclusion.range_basis: No exact project target-zone counties are currently locked. Statewide Texas nativity, Trans-Pecos occurrence, and the common name are not converted into county proof.

approval_exception.reason: Learner inclusion is independent from native-range certification.

best_field_traits: source conflict: Kew reports annual; 2024 taxonomic treatment reports herbaceous perennial — do NOT use life history for identification
exactly one leaflet pair per compound leaf
leaflets relatively broad, about 1.3–1.8 times as long as wide
mixture of short retrorse hairs, glandlike trichomes and longer stiff setae on stems
extrafloral gland at the point where the paired leaflets join
persistent sepals on developing fruit; anthers constricted below symmetric terminal pollen pore
erect oblong pods roughly 2–4 cm long, hairy/setose; can persist after opening
morphology_keys.comparison_training: S. roemeriana also has one leaflet pair, but its leaflets are much more narrowly lanceolate (approximately 2–9 times as long as wide). S. bauhinioides also has a single broad pair; distinguish with stiff mixed stem hairs, persistent sepals, anther/pod detail, and S. bauhinioides stout thickened style + rough seed testa. Life history, leaflet count alone and yellow flowers do not separate this trio.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Broad paired leaflets + retrorse hairs and stiff setae versus narrow paired leaflets in S. roemeriana; against S. bauhinioides, use floral style/anther and mature pod/seed plus indumentum; retain uncertain ID if no reproductive material.
